roles.title: Australia Community Engagement Internship
roles.location: Lake Macquarie, New South Wales, Australia
roles.description: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the Australia Team Zipline is building its presence in Australia, and we are looking for an exceptional student or recent graduate to join the team as a part-time Australia Expansion Fellow. The Australia team is responsible for developing the partnerships, market strategy and operations required to bring Zipline’s autonomous logistics system to communities across the country. This means working at the intersection of business, government, technology and community to understand where Zipline can have the greatest impact and what it will take to get there. The Role As an Australia Expansion Fellow, you will work directly with Zipline’s Head of Australia on our community engagement strategy. This is a hands-on role. You’ll spend time with our local leadership out in the community, meeting residents, businesses and community organisations, listening to their perspectives and ensuring questions and concerns are addressed. You will help translate our exciting but unfamiliar technology into clear, credible and locally relevant conversations. Success means communities hear from Zipline early, have meaningful opportunities to engage with us, and see the benefits of having Zipline operate in their community. The ideal candidate is intellectually curious, an excellent communicator, and highly attuned to community sentiment. What You'll Do Build relationships with residents, community groups, elected officials, local businesses and environmental organisations Engage local influencers, community publishers and social media group administrators Organise community briefings, listening sessions, demonstrations, open days and retailer events Explain Zipline’s technology clearly and credibly, including addressing concerns such as noise and safety Monitor community sentiment and identify emerging concerns early Manage stakeholder outreach, follow-ups and the community CRM Bring community feedback back into Zipline and help teams respond to what we hear Represent Zipline at local meetings, events and community forums What You'll Bring Experience in community engagement, stakeholder relations, public affairs or a related field A strong track record of building trusted relationships with local communities Excellent communication, listening and relationship-building skills Confidence engaging with everyone from residents and small-business owners to councillors and MPs The ability to explain complex or technical topics simply Good judgement and confidence in handling challenging questions or concerns Ability to take ownership of ambiguous problems and work independently Knowledge of the Central Coast and Lake Macquarie regions would be a significant advantage A practical, energetic approach and willingness to spend time out in the community, including some evenings and events Genuine interest in Zipline’s mission and a passionate belief in the benefits our drone delivery technology can bring to communities What Else You Should Know This fellowship is a part-time, hybrid position based in the Sydney, Central Coast or Lake Macquarie areas. The hourly rate for this fellowship is $50 AUD per hour. Please note that this is a target cash rate for a candidate who meets the minimum qualifications for this role. The final cash pay for this role will depend on a variety of factors, including a specific candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, and working location. Additional benefits may include paid sick time and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. roles.description: Come join one of America’s fastest-growing insurance companies. Since 1848, National Life Group has aimed to keep our promises, providing families with stability in good times and in bad. Throughout that history, we have provided peace of mind to those families as they plan their futures. Our mission extends beyond the insurance and annuities policies that we offer. We strive to make the world a better place through our grants from our charitable foundation, paid volunteer time for our employees, environmentally sustainable and healthy workplaces, and events that promote the work of nonprofits in our own backyard. We foster a collaborative environment with opportunities for growth and encourage our associates to live our values: Do good. Be good. Make good. Please note that we do not offer visa sponsorship for this position. POSITION SUMMARY: At National Life Group, we are modernizing our business and adapting our customer experience to a digital-first operating model. We aim to activate, engage, inspire, and connect with buying and selling customers to increase production, deepen relationships, and create meaningful connections grounded in our mission and purpose. Measuring progress and performance through meaningful insights is central to our transformation. The Capital Management internship will provide exposure to how a leading U.S. life and annuity insurer evaluates current and projected capital needs, understanding the drivers of changes in capital and risk-based capital ratios, and provide insight into potential capital impacts from business activities, investment decisions, reinsurance deals, and regulatory developments. The intern will collaborate cross-functionally across Finance, Accounting, Actuarial, Risk Management, Investments, and other corporate teams. The Capital Management Intern will support the company’s efforts to monitor, analyze, forecast, and manage its financial strength, capital position, and risks by assisting with updating and validating capital models, analyzing and forecasting changes in regulatory and rating-agency capital, and understanding and communicating capital implications for the company, in addition to activities such as process improvements and documentation activities. This position currently offers an onsite work schedule, with the expectation that you will be in the office four (4) days per week during onsite core days. Our current onsite core days are Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday. The work schedule type and core days are subject to change with advance notification and manager discretion. RESPONSIBILITIES: Update capital analysis on a quarterly and as-needed basis, including data population, error resolution, interpreting results, and preparing presentation materials Assist in the preparation of quarterly Risk-Based Capital (“RBC”) calculation and attribution analysis, including validating and summarizing results Perform impact analysis of proposed regulatory capital changes for RBC and S&P model Collaborate with internal partners to perform assigned duties Improve efficiency of working files and processes Document capital management processes and procedures Perform ad hoc analysis and provide support for capital management activities, responsibilities and communications All other duties as assigned MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: Pursuing degree in Finance, Actuarial Studies, Math, or a similar quantitative field Experience with gathering, organizing, cleaning, and interpreting information (e.g. data sets) Working exposure with relational databases (e.g. Microsoft SQL, Access) and writing queries Working exposure using Analytical and Visualization tools, specifically Tableau & Alteryx Ability to translate business needs into effective analytical solutions and models Understanding of foundational financial principles, e.g. interest rates, investments, and financial statements (e.g. balance sheet) Strong analytical skills with the ability to work in a fast-paced finance environment Ability to meet deadlines for recurring reporting and analysis Ability to quickly develop professional relationships with others and effectively communicate using various platforms or methods Proficiency in Microsoft Office, e.g. Excel AI Proficiency Expectations At National Life Group, we view AI as an enabler of human potential. We use AI to help us work smarter, serve more clients, and keep our promises, while remaining a relationship-driven business where our people are our greatest strength. All associates are expected to: Leverage approved AI tools, where appropriate, to improve the efficiency, quality, and impact of their work. Stay curious and open to new AI-enabled ways of working. Exercise sound judgment by reviewing and validating AI-generated content. Maintain accountability for the accuracy, quality, fairness, and integrity of work products by adhering to National Life's AI guiding principles. Unlike a traditional internship, Impact Works offers the opportunity to rotate among multiple nonprofit partners, gaining hands-on experience with a variety of missions, projects, and community needs. Throughout the summer, you'll support short-term assignments ranging from communications and marketing to event planning, volunteer coordination, grant research, and organizational support. Each assignment offers a new opportunity to develop professional skills, build relationships, and experience firsthand the important role nonprofits play in our communities. Develop communications and marketing materials, including social media content, newsletters, digital graphics, and event promotions. Support nonprofit operations through research, data organization, grant prospecting, and administrative projects. Quickly learn each organization's goals and priorities, adapting to new environments and delivering quality work within short timelines. Required Experience and Skills: Pursuing a degree in Communications, Marketing, Journalism, Public Relations, Business, Nonprofit Management, or a related field preferred. Excellent organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects and meet deadlines. Self-motivated, adaptable, and comfortable taking initiative, asking questions, and working independently. Creative thinker with strong problem-solving skills and a collaborative mindset. roles.description: Compensation and Benefits Analyst Intern Location: San Jose, California, United States Employment type: Internship About the role We are looking for a Compensation and Benefits Analyst Intern to join the Total Rewards team and help support thoughtful, data-informed compensation and benefits programs. This is a hands-on opportunity to learn how compensation structures, market data, benefits operations, HR systems, and employee-facing programs work together. You will work with Total Rewards, HR Operations, Finance, Payroll, HR Business Partners, and other stakeholders to organize information, analyze data, document processes, and move defined projects forward. Prepare Excel-based analyses, reports, dashboards, presentations, and data-backed summaries for Total Rewards and HR stakeholders. Assist with recurring compensation and benefits activities by maintaining trackers, documenting assumptions, monitoring milestones, and following up on open items. Support benefits operations by organizing plan information, employee-facing materials, vendor or process documentation, and questions routed to the appropriate team. Help review HR and compensation data for completeness, consistency, accuracy, and appropriate access; investigate discrepancies and escalate questions with context. Maintain process documentation, reference materials, checklists, workpapers, and project records so recurring activities are clear and repeatable. Support HR systems and data workflows by documenting requirements, validating outputs, tracking changes, and identifying opportunities to improve reporting or data quality. Partner with Total Rewards, HR Operations, Finance, Payroll, HR Business Partners, and other cross-functional stakeholders to clarify needs and communicate progress. Help identify opportunities to simplify reporting, improve employee or stakeholder experiences, and make compensation and benefits processes more efficient. Contribute to process-improvement or automation efforts by researching use cases, documenting requirements, tracking milestones, and reporting outcomes. Work with sensitive compensation, benefits, employee, and business information in accordance with team expectations for confidentiality and data handling. Own a defined internship project with mentor support, demonstrate measurable progress, deliver implementable work, and present data-backed results and recommendations at the end of the internship. What you bring Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in human resources, business, finance, economics, statistics, data analytics, mathematics, or a related field. Strong analytical and quantitative skills, with careful attention to detail and data accuracy. Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint, including the ability to organize data and communicate analysis clearly. Ability to learn new systems and processes, work with structured and unstructured information, and keep projects moving. Strong written and verbal communication skills and comfort collaborating with cross-functional partners. Sound judgment, discretion, and maturity when handling confidential compensation, benefits, employee, and business information. Organization, ownership, curiosity, flexibility, and willingness to ask questions and learn. Ability to manage milestones and deadlines, follow through reliably, and adapt when project scope or priorities change. Preferred qualifications Coursework or project experience in compensation, benefits, human resources, finance, accounting, statistics, survey analysis, data visualization, or business analytics. Experience creating Excel analyses, trackers, dashboards, process documentation, presentations, or other business-facing materials. Familiarity with HR information systems, compensation or benefits data, benchmarking, employee surveys, or reporting workflows. Interest in process improvement, automation, and how technology can improve Total Rewards analysis and operations. roles.title: Global Supply Management Intern (Spring 2027)
roles.description: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the Global Supply Management Team The Global Supply Management Team ensures that Zipline has the parts it needs from suppliers around the world in a reliable, sustainable, and cost-effective way. We build and maintain strong relationships with suppliers, negotiate contracts, and monitor supplier performance to reduce supply risk. The team also works closely with the design engineering, supplier industrial engineering, finance, program management, and material management teams to understand part design, manage supply against demand, drive cost reductions, and streamline logistics across international markets. The Role As a Global Supply Management Intern, you’ll gain hands-on exposure to the systems, data, and supplier relationships that power Zipline’s global supply chain. You’ll work alongside supply managers, engineers, finance, and operations teams to support sourcing, analytics, and day-to-day execution. This role is perfect for a student to apply classroom knowledge to real-world challenges in procurement, logistics, and global operations. Your work will directly support Zipline’s mission to deliver essential goods and services across the world while building critical skills in supply chain management. What You'll Do Assist in tracking and analyzing supplier performance, purchase orders, and delivery timelines. Prepare reports, dashboards, and presentations on supply chain metrics. Support sourcing activities by gathering quotes, conducting supplier research, and benchmarking costs. Work with internal stakeholders to troubleshoot supply issues and identify process improvements. Participate in supplier meetings and cross-functional discussions to gain exposure to real-world negotiations and decision-making. Document and standardize processes to help build scalable systems. What You'll Bring Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; comfortable working with spreadsheets (Excel/Google Sheets). Curiosity and eagerness to learn about global supply chain operations in a fast-paced environment. Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work on cross-functional projects. Organizational skills and attention to detail, with a willingness to dive into both strategic and tactical tasks. Preferred majors: Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business, Economics. What Else You Should Know Our internships are full-time positions, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from January 2027 to April/May 2027. The hourly rate for this internship is $37 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period. Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. Voluntary Self-Identification For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

roles.title: Human Factors (Winter Co-Op)
roles.description: At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. ROLE OVERVIEW: A seaglider floats, foils, and flies — and every one of those transitions has to make sense to the pilots flying it and the passengers riding in it. Nobody has designed that interface before. As a Human Factors Co-Op, you’ll help shape it: contributing to concept sketches, UI/UX standards, and the usability evaluations that keep the interface safe, intuitive, and ready for certification. As part of the Systems team, you’ll be joining a group of driven, collaborative, and talented engineers who take pride in solving complex technical challenges and making an impact as a team. We hold a high bar for engineering rigor, move quickly, think boldly, and rely on our teamwork to push boundaries and bring entirely new technology into the world. If you’d rather sketch and test a real interface than read about one, and you want hands-on experience on a vehicle nobody has built before, we’d love to have you on the team! What You'll Do: - Contribute to new feature concepts. Bring ideas for how pilots and passengers interact with the seaglider human interface. - Help build out our design standards. Contribute to REGENT’s UI/UX standards and design language. - Support safety and usability evaluations. Help plan and run evaluations of the seaglider human interface. - Help define human factors requirements. Support requirements definition and draft test procedures. - Partner across engineering disciplines. Work with engineers across systems, software, and flight test to bring HF findings into the design. What We’re Looking For: - Working toward a relevant degree. Pursuing a degree in Human Factors Engineering, Engineering Psychology, or a related field. - Some exposure to aviation or maritime contexts. Coursework, research, or personal flying, boating, or sailing experience. - Comfort with prototyping and communication. Proficiency with rapid prototyping tools (e.g., Figma); excellent written and verbal communication, including technical documentation. - Self-motivated and adaptable. Comfortable with shifting priorities in a startup environment. Who We’re Looking For: - Curious about people, not just tech. You want to know why someone struggles with an interface, not just that they do, and you’re excited to go find out firsthand. - Hands-on, not just theoretical. You’d rather sketch a quick mockup or run a small usability test than write a memo about what one might find. - Comfortable without a precedent. A seaglider cockpit doesn’t look like anything that exists yet. You’re energized by that, not looking for a template to follow. - Present for the work. Evaluations and test days don’t always land on a tidy schedule, and you’re ready to show up when the work needs you. WHAT WE OFFER - Competitive compensation - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team - Daily, free catered lunches - Learning & professional development opportunities - Meaningful projects that make an impact - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact. Equal Opportunity Employer REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

roles.title: Inventory Management Intern
roles.description: Instawork is on a mission to create meaningful economic opportunities for skilled hourly professionals in communities around the globe. Our AI-powered labor marketplace helps local businesses scale, and enables global technology companies to push the frontiers of robotics and AI. Backed by world-class investors like Benchmark, Spark Capital, Craft Ventures, Greylock, Y Combinator, and others, we’re looking for exceptional talent to reimagine the way the world works. Inventory Manager – High Value Devices Function: Operations – Asset & Inventory Control Inventory Type: High-Value Electronic Assets Tools Used: Manual Registers & Google Sheets Work Mode: On-site Role Overview The Inventory Manager will be responsible for end-to-end custody, tracking, and reconciliation of high-value inventory, primarily iPhones and related accessories such as SD cards and card readers. This role demands strict control, zero tolerance for mismatches, and complete documentation discipline. No inventory movement is allowed without entries, and physical stock must always tally with records. (Morning Shift - 7 am to 4 pm; Evening Shift - 4 pm to 2 am) Key Responsibilities 1. High-Value Inventory Ownership Take complete ownership of high-value devices and accessories . Ensure serial-number–level tracking for all devices. Maintain zero loss and zero undocumented movement . 2. Inward Inventory Management (IT → Inventory) Receive devices and accessories from the IT team. Verify: Quantity Serial numbers Physical condition Record all inward movements immediately in: Manual registers Google Sheets Escalate any mismatch, damage, or discrepancy without delay. 3. Outward Inventory Management (Inventory ↔ Field Ops) Hand over inventory from: Inventory to Field Ops (FO) Field Ops back to Inventory Ensure no item goes out without prior entry . Capture details including: Item name and serial number FO name / ID Date and time of handover Expected return date Avoid all verbal or informal handovers. 4. Returns, Reconciliation & Control Receive returned inventory and re-verify serial numbers and condition. Update return entries on the same day. Perform daily reconciliation between: Physical stock Google Sheets Items with Field Ops Track overdue or missing items and follow up proactively. 5. Documentation & Audit Readiness Maintain clean, structured Google Sheets trackers. Ensure inventory area access is controlled. Support audits and internal checks as required. Maintain high compliance standards for asset handling. Skills & Requirements Mandatory Experience handling high-value inventory or assets . Strong working knowledge of Google Sheets (filters, basic formulas). Experience with manual inventory registers . High attention to detail and accuracy. Preferred Background in inventory, warehouse, logistics, or operations. Experience managing electronic devices or serialized assets. Key Traits Strong ownership and accountability Process-driven with a zero-error mindset High integrity and discipline Comfortable working under strict controls Performance Metrics 100% match between physical inventory and records Zero undocumented inventory movement Zero asset loss due to process lapses Timely reconciliation and reporting Our Values Empathy, Trust & Candor We put ourselves in the shoes of our colleagues and customers and don’t shy away from uncomfortable conversations, instead building trust through honest and direct feedback. Bias for Action We practice high-velocity decision-making, clear-eyed that we often operate with incomplete information. Growing quickly means it’s OK to be wrong, so long as we learn from our mistakes and course correct! Always Be Learning We’re a curious bunch, and with AI transforming our workplace we encourage everyone to learn from each other, compounding our knowledge and experience to help us change an entire industry. Act Like an Owner We work long, hard, and smart, building products that delight our users and drive growth. Your ability to impact Instawork is limited only by your courage and conviction, not your job description. About Instawork Founded in 2015, Instawork is the nation’s leading online labor marketplace for food services, hospitality, light industry, and logistics, connecting more than 7M skilled workers with local restaurants, hotels, warehouses, stadiums, and more. Our AI-powered platform serves thousands of businesses across more than 50 major markets in the United States and Canada. We're not just helping fill shifts, we're supporting local economies—and we're just getting started! Instawork has been featured by CBS News, The Wall Street Journal, The Washington Post, and the Associated Press. Forbes included us on their Next Billion Dollar Startups list; RetailTech Breakthrough named us Workforce Hiring Solution of the Year for 2025; and Inc. 5000 recognized us as one of the country's top 10% fastest-growing companies two years in a row. But what matters most is our impact. We're solving real problems for real people, and we’re doing it at scale. Join our team to help us build something that matters! We’re looking for superstars who want to help us shape the future of work. With hubs in San Francisco, Bangalore, and Chicago, city offices in New York and Phoenix, we're back to working together in-person five days a week because we believe the best ideas happen when great people collaborate face-to-face. We also value diverse perspectives and encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds. Ready to make an impact? Learn more at www.instawork.com/about . Personnel Privacy Policy

roles.title: Nigeria Recruitment Intern
roles.description: About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. The Nigeria program, established in 2018, is headquartered in Minna, Niger state. We're currently serving over 100,000 unique farmers across the state via our inputs on credit 'Core' program, inputs on cash 'Retail' program, and have a free tree seedling distribution 'Agroforestry' program. To learn more about our work, look at our Nigeria program blog. About the Young Professionals Program One Acre Fund’s Young Professionals Program offers high-performing African graduates meaningful internships and training opportunities at a high-performing, mission-driven organization. Our internships are paid and all interns can expect to receive substantive work assignments working on high-impact projects that support One Acre Fund's operations. When joining, interns will participate in an onboarding program and receive training on how to design and execute projects. Over the period of your internship, you will get the opportunity to work with like-minded individuals and receive learning opportunities to build strong foundations for your future career. About the Role Seeking a curious, eager to learn professional to kickstart their recruitment career by mastering the "engine room" of our hiring processes and driving a world-class candidate experience. Responsibilities Operational Excellence: You will execute recurring administrative tasks to keep recruitment operations running smoothly, ensuring 100% data accuracy in all trackers and documentation. Candidate Experience: You will facilitate the candidate screening process, including CV longlisting and interview scheduling, and provide professional, timely communication to ensure every candidate has the best experience. ATS Management: You will maintain the candidate database (Applicant Tracking System), ensuring all applicant statuses are up to date and helping extract basic data for weekly reporting. Continuous Improvement: In collaboration with your manager, you will assist in identifying bottlenecks in the recruitment flow and support the rollout of new tools or process updates. Logistics/Coordination: You will manage the logistics for interview panels, ensuring all interviewers have the necessary materials and candidates are well-briefed. Contribute to ad-hoc projects and provide operational support to the Team as required. Career Growth and Development We have a strong culture of constant learning and we deeply invest in our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training, and regular feedback on your performance. We’ll hold career reviews every one-three months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and gain rewarding technical experience. Qualifications Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for . For this role specifically, you will have: Bachelor’s degree in any relevant field of study. 6 months to 1 year of recruitment or HR experience, preferably in a fast-paced environment, and passionate about the work we do at One Acre Fund for Smallholder Farmers. Familiarity with Google Workspace and Applicant Tracking Systems (e.g., Greenhouse) is a plus. Basic data analysis skills - you can pick out patterns. Great learning skills, curious, and a knack for attention to detail. A strong communicator who can collaborate effectively with different stakeholders. Proficiency in English is required. Preferred Start Date As soon as possible Job Location Abuja, Nigeria. Benefits Interns will be provided with a reasonable stipend for the duration of their contract. Eligibility This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Nigeria. Application Deadline 30 December 2026. We hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made. One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @ oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here ( globalhotline@oneacrefund.org ), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address. Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

HillelU provides learning and development opportunities to more than 1,200 Hillel professionals across the organization. As our portfolio continues to grow, this role will provide the operational support needed to deliver high-quality professional development experiences consistently and efficiently—from virtual training and cohort programs to immersive in-person leadership development experiences. This role will serve as a key member of the Talent Development & Training team, taking ownership of the systems, logistics, data, and processes that support the participant experience. The ideal candidate is someone who loves turning plans into action, can anticipate details before they become problems, and is energized by making complex programs feel seamless. What You’ll Do Program Operations & Delivery Support the operational execution of assigned HillelU programs and learning experiences, from initial planning through post-program follow-up. Coordinate session setup, registration, materials, technology, and other operational needs. Manage pre- and post-program communications, including reminders, pre-work, and logistics. Provide or coordinate day-of technology and administrative support for virtual and in-person programs. Partner with facilitators and Talent Development colleagues to ensure they have the information and support needed for successful program delivery. Create and maintain repeatable processes, templates, and checklists that make program delivery more efficient and consistent. Identify operational challenges and proactively develop solutions. Program Data, Evaluation & Reporting Collect, organize, maintain and report on participation and program data. Pull and upload data across relevant systems and ensure program records remain accurate and up to date. Coordinate post-program evaluation processes, including evaluation communications and data collection. Develop regular reports and dashboards that help the Talent Development team understand participation, engagement, and program outcomes. Support analysis of program data to identify trends and inform future planning and decision-making. Partner with colleagues to improve how HillelU tracks and communicates program impact. Leadership Development & Event Logistics Support the operational delivery of select high-touch programs and experiences, including Kaplan Supervisory Leadership Program and Accelerate. Coordinate event logistics including hotels, catering, travel, participant communications, materials, schedules, and other event needs. Manage participant travel reimbursements and other program-related expenses. Coordinate across facilitators, participants, vendors, internal partners, and other stakeholders to ensure a seamless experience. Provide on-site operational support for select HillelU professional development experiences, as needed. Systems & Process Improvement Maintain systems for tracking HillelU programs, participants, logistics, and outcomes. Look for opportunities to streamline administrative processes and reduce manual work. Create documentation and standard operating procedures to support consistency and continuity across the HillelU portfolio. Help the team leverage technology and data more effectively in the delivery and evaluation of learning programs. Support implementation of new tools, systems, and processes as HillelU continues to evolve. Team Partnership Serve as a collaborative operational partner to Talent Development colleagues, helping translate program ideas into executable plans. Support multiple concurrent projects and priorities while maintaining a high level of attention to detail. Provide visibility into project status, upcoming deadlines, and operational needs. Take ownership of projects and follow through independently while knowing when to escalate questions or challenges. Contribute to a collaborative, positive, and service-oriented team culture. Who You Are Highly organized and detail-oriented , with the ability to manage many moving pieces without losing sight of the big picture. A strong project manager who can establish timelines, track details, and ensure work moves forward. Proactive and solutions-oriented , with a natural instinct to anticipate needs and troubleshoot challenges. A strong communicator who can build relationships and communicate clearly with a wide range of stakeholders. Comfortable with technology and data , and excited to learn new systems and tools. Service-oriented , with a strong commitment to creating excellent experiences for participants, facilitators, and colleagues. Able to work independently , take ownership, and exercise good judgment. Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment with multiple simultaneous priorities. Proficient in Google Workspace and Microsoft Office; experience with Salesforce, Zoom, learning management systems, event platforms, or similar tools is a plus. We encourage both current college students and recent graduates to apply for this role. What You’ll Receive $17/hr up to 20 hours/week In this role, you’ll gain hands-on experience in program operations, project coordination, data and evaluation, event logistics, and talent development while working alongside a team that designs and delivers professional development for Hillel professionals across the organization. You’ll have the opportunity to see how learning experiences are designed, delivered, evaluated, and improved and to build skills that translate across nonprofit, education, Human Resources, and business environments. About Hillel International In 1923, Rabbi Benjamin Frankel started Hillel with humble means, a noble mission and a breathtaking vision: to convey Jewish civilization to a new generation. Today, Hillel International continues to enrich the lives of Jewish students and is the largest Jewish campus organization in the world at nearly 1,000 colleges and universities across North America and around the world. As Hillel evolves as an organization, the mission remains steadfast: to create lasting connections with every Jewish student that foster an enduring commitment to Jewish life, learning, and Israel and train them to become the next Jewish leaders. Hillel is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an accepting and inclusive environment for all.

roles.title: Operations Management Intern
roles.description: Instawork is on a mission to create meaningful economic opportunities for skilled hourly professionals in communities around the globe. Our AI-powered labor marketplace helps local businesses scale, and enables global technology companies to push the frontiers of robotics and AI. Backed by world-class investors like Benchmark, Spark Capital, Craft Ventures, Greylock, Y Combinator, and others, we’re looking for exceptional talent to reimagine the way the world works. Instawork is on a mission to create meaningful economic opportunities for skilled hourly professionals in communities around the globe. Our AI-powered labor marketplace helps local businesses scale, and enables global technology companies to push the frontiers of robotics and AI. Backed by world-class investors like Benchmark, Spark Capital, Craft Ventures, Greylock, Y Combinator, and others, we're looking for exceptional talent to reimagine the way the world works. Role Overview An Internal Coordinator (IC) owns the day-to-day running of field data collection for a single region. Each IC leads a team of Field Officers (FOs) who carry recording rigs(hardware) into partner businesses, set them up correctly, and capture high-quality task recordings. The IC is the operational nerve center of the region: planning the day's pipeline, keeping FOs productive in the field, solving problems live, ensuring recording quality and diversity rules are met, tracking inventory (rigs and SD cards) in and out, and reporting hours planned vs. achieved with clear loss reasons at end of day. This role is mainly about live coordination, field problem-solving, quality control, and disciplined reporting. Who Are Field Officers (FOs)? People working on the ground, out in the field They collect rigs from inventory, travel to assigned businesses, and record short videos of real commercial/household tasks They are responsible for correct setup, on-site recording, and returning rigs and SD cards They have clear daily and overall hour targets to complete Key Responsibilities 1. Start-of-Day Planning Check the day's pipeline of confirmed businesses for each FO Keep enough backup businesses on hand so no FO is left idle if a task falls through Confirm rig, SD card, and inventory availability before FOs leave Plan for exigencies (business cancellations, FO absence, device shortfall, travel issues) 2. Live Monitoring & 2-Hourly Updates Track who has started, who is on-site, who is recording, and who is falling behind Take structured updates from every FO at least every 2 hours to catch and solve issues early Follow up immediately with FOs who are idle, delayed, or stuck 3. Target & Productivity Management Ensure FOs meet their daily and overall hour targets Redirect FOs to backup businesses when a planned task drops, to protect the day's hours Push and motivate the team to close the day on plan 4. Quality, Rules & Diversity Adherence Ensure FOs follow recording rules: correct task type, valid duration, correct rig/camera setup Verify setup quality before recording begins — e.g. confirm camera alignment via screenshots so the rig is capturing correctly before the task runs Ensure recordings respect diversity caps (per-operator and per-environment limits) so hours actually count as usable Work with the Quality team to understand where recordings are failing, and retrain FOs to record better-quality, usable data 5. Issue Resolution Act as the first point of contact for FOs in the field Help resolve: app/upload issues, task confusion, "business saying no," "task not legit enough," and device/rig issues (coordinate with Field Ops / Inventory / Hardware teams as needed) Escalate only when an issue can't be solved at your level 6. Inventory & Asset Tracking Track every rig and SD card issued to each FO — out and back Reconcile returns the same day; follow up proactively on anything overdue or missing Flag damage, loss, or undocumented movement without delay 7. Communication & Coordination Manage large WhatsApp groups of FOs for the region Share daily instructions, reminders, and updates Maintain discipline and professionalism in groups 8. End-of-Day Reporting Report hours planned vs. achieved for the region Detail loss reasons clearly and by category — e.g. hardware/rig breakdown, business declined, task not legitimate, FO/travel issues, quality rejections Share a clean daily status summary with the Field Ops Manager Skills & Requirements Basic computer knowledge Comfortable using WhatsApp and Google Sheets Ability to manage and communicate with many people at once Strong coordination, multitasking, and real-time problem-solving skills Comfort reading simple operational data (hours, targets, loss reasons) Personal Qualities Alert and responsible Patient but firm Organized and disciplined Comfortable working in a fast-paced, on-ground operations environment Role Scale 1 IC manages a region of Field Officers High-responsibility, field-operations-focused role Reports to the Team lead of Operations Our Values Empathy, Trust & Candor We put ourselves in the shoes of our colleagues and customers and don’t shy away from uncomfortable conversations, instead building trust through honest and direct feedback. Bias for Action We practice high-velocity decision-making, clear-eyed that we often operate with incomplete information. Growing quickly means it’s OK to be wrong, so long as we learn from our mistakes and course correct! Always Be Learning We’re a curious bunch, and with AI transforming our workplace we encourage everyone to learn from each other, compounding our knowledge and experience to help us change an entire industry. Act Like an Owner We work long, hard, and smart, building products that delight our users and drive growth. Your ability to impact Instawork is limited only by your courage and conviction, not your job description. About Instawork Founded in 2015, Instawork is the nation’s leading online labor marketplace for food services, hospitality, light industry, and logistics, connecting more than 7M skilled workers with local restaurants, hotels, warehouses, stadiums, and more. Our AI-powered platform serves thousands of businesses across more than 50 major markets in the United States and Canada. We're not just helping fill shifts, we're supporting local economies—and we're just getting started! Instawork has been featured by CBS News, The Wall Street Journal, The Washington Post, and the Associated Press. Forbes included us on their Next Billion Dollar Startups list; RetailTech Breakthrough named us Workforce Hiring Solution of the Year for 2025; and Inc. 5000 recognized us as one of the country's top 10% fastest-growing companies two years in a row. But what matters most is our impact. We're solving real problems for real people, and we’re doing it at scale. Join our team to help us build something that matters! We’re looking for superstars who want to help us shape the future of work. With hubs in San Francisco, Bangalore, and Chicago, city offices in New York and Phoenix, we're back to working together in-person five days a week because we believe the best ideas happen when great people collaborate face-to-face. We also value diverse perspectives and encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds. Ready to make an impact? Learn more at www.instawork.com/about . Personnel Privacy Policy

roles.title: Payroll & Benefits Intern (Practicante de Nómina y Compensación)
roles.description: The salary for the Payroll & Benefits Intern is $2.800.000 COP monthly. About Sezzle With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We're not just transforming payments; we're redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we're building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you're excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping! About the Role As a Payroll & Benefits Intern, you'll join our People Operations team and work directly with our Senior Director of Payroll & Benefits. You'll see how payroll, compensation, and benefits run across Colombia, the United States, and Canada inside a fast-growing, publicly traded fintech. This is a paid, learning-focused internship with a clear path to full-time conversion based on performance. We are seeking a talented and motivated intern who is best in class with a high IQ plus a high EQ. No prior payroll experience is required; attention to detail, curiosity, and a good head for numbers matter more. What You'll Do Help run monthly payroll: data entry, reconciliations, and documentation Keep payroll, benefits, and HR system data accurate, and flag anything that doesn't match Support benefits enrollments, changes, and employee records Help prepare documents for monthly, quarterly, and year-end audits Gather market data for compensation benchmarking Answer employee questions about payroll and benefits Spot manual steps we can automate, including testing new AI tools What You'll Learn How multi-country payroll works, from Colombian labor law to US payroll and benefits rules (FLSA, ACA, ERISA, COBRA) How companies benchmark and set compensation How People Operations supports a company's growth, including Sezzle's bank charter readiness What We Look For Current university student or recent graduate in Accounting (Contaduría Pública), Finance, Economics, Business Administration, Industrial Engineering, or a related field Strong attention to detail and comfort working with numbers Good Excel or Google Sheets skills English proficiency (written and spoken), since you'll work daily with US-based teams Native or near-native Spanish Discretion with confidential information Comfortable using AI tools such as Claude or ChatGPT to boost productivity, research, and communication Nice to Have Coursework or basic knowledge of Colombian payroll, taxes, or labor regulations Interest in automation and process improvement About You You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed. You're not bound by convention - your success—and much of the fun—lies in developing new ways to do things. You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking. You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully. You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting. You have conviction and are tenacious. You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly. You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle. What Makes Working at Sezzle Awesome At Sezzle, we are more than just brilliant engineers, passionate data enthusiasts, out-of-the-box thinkers, and determined innovators. We believe in surrounding ourselves with only the best and the brightest individuals. Our culture is not defined by a certain set of perks designed to give the illusion of the traditional startup culture, but rather, it is the visible example living in every employee that we hire. #Li-remote #Full-time

roles.title: People & Culture Intern Spring 2027
roles.description: ABOUT ROCKET LAB Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us. As a People and Culture Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Long Beach, California, you will have the opportunity to gain hands-on experience in People & Culture operations and insight into our company's approach to the employee life cycle. The team collaborates closely with Total Rewards, TA, EIS, Security, Payroll, EH&S, IT, Facilities, and Legal to support daily operations. WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO As an intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees within the department to apply your knowledge and grow your skills both technically and professionally Work with a fast-paced group of professionals to apply engineering and industry concepts to solve real challenges Attend frequent 1:1’s with mentors and supervisors to facilitate success and learning while providing progress updates Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate program in Business Administration, Human Resources, Management or related field and have at least one semester of school remaining post internship. GPA of 3.0 or above. 3+ months of corporate function experience within the areas of Human Resources. THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE GPA of 3.5 or above. 6+ months of corporate function experience within the areas of Human Resources. Strong experience with Microsoft Office (Powerpoint & Excel) Strong time management skills and attentive to details ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning January, February, or March 2027 COMPENSATION AND OTHER BENEFITS Pay Range CA: $25.00 USD Hourly You may be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience. Base salary is just one component of our total rewards package at Rocket Lab. Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match. Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts. Eligibility for benefits may vary based on employment status, please check with your recruiter for a comprehensive list of the benefits available for this role. Benefit programs are subject to change at the company’s discretion. Hourly Pay Range (CA Only) $25 — $25 USD WHAT TO EXPECT We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way. Important information: FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY: To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. Learn more about ITAR here . Rocket Lab provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment at Rocket Lab, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training. Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for the application/interview process for a job in the United States should contact Giulia Johnson at g.biow@rocketlabusa.com. This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days. FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY: For security reasons, background checks will be undertaken prior to any employment offers being made to an applicant. These checks will include nationality checks as it is a requirement of this position that you be eligible to access equipment and data regulated by the United States' International Traffic in Arms Regulations. Under these Regulations, you may be ineligible for this role if you do not hold citizenship of Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, the European Union, or a country that is part of NATO, or if you hold ineligible dual citizenship or nationality. For more information on these Regulations, click here ITAR Regulations.

roles.description: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? Coinbase is building the future of finance for people, institutions and their agents, with one place to trade crypto, equities, derivatives and prediction markets, use stablecoins, and connect AI agents with clear controls. The bar is high and the pace is intense, and we like it that way. This isn’t a place for complacency. It’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits and do the best work of your career. If you’re ready to build the future of finance with a championship team who refuse to settle for “good enough,” you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for in-person working sessions This is a 12-week internship during summer 2027. You'll join the People Analytics team within our People Success Function. This team provides intelligence and tools that empower leaders to make key people decisions and drive business value. You'll support analyses across the employee lifecycle, help streamline reporting processes, and contribute to solutions that measure the impact of complex People programs. What you'll do: Analyze People data across the employee lifecycle to identify trends and surface actionable insights for leadership Apply AI tools to accelerate data exploration and enable self-service access to insights for stakeholders Prototype AI-driven workflow automations for recurring reports, anomaly detection, and data-quality checks Support ad hoc data requests by building and maintaining spreadsheets and dashboards Partner with stakeholders to improve dashboard navigation, access, and self-service reporting Collaborate with team members to develop executive presentations that translate data into clear narratives Required Skills and Experience: Currently pursuing a degree or certificate in an analytical discipline (e.g., data science, statistics, I/O psychology, business analytics, or related field). Proven ability to communicate data insights clearly in both written and verbal formats to non-technical audiences. Track record of handling highly sensitive or confidential data with discretion. Familiarity with at least one data visualization tool (Looker, Tableau, PowerBI, or OneModel) or basic SQL knowledge is a plus. Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality Position ID: P78055 #LI-Hybrid Pay Transparency Notice: Depending on your work location, the target hourly rate for this position can range as detailed below. roles.title: People Center Intern – Summer 2027
roles.description: Come join one of America’s fastest-growing insurance companies. Since 1848, National Life Group has aimed to keep our promises, providing families with stability in good times and in bad. Throughout that history, we have provided peace of mind to those families as they plan their futures. Our mission extends beyond the insurance and annuities policies that we offer. We strive to make the world a better place through our grants from our charitable foundation, paid volunteer time for our employees, environmentally sustainable and healthy workplaces, and events that promote the work of nonprofits in our own backyard. We foster a collaborative environment with opportunities for growth and encourage our associates to live our values: Do good. Be good. Make good. Please note that we do not offer visa sponsorship for this position POSITION SUMMARY: As an intern in the People Center, you will have the opportunity to learn about each of the critical functions within Human Resources that shape the employee experience at National Life. You will rotate through two areas of the People Center, gaining hands on experience in Talent Acquisition, Learning & Organizational Development. Throughout this rotation, you will work on meaningful projects that impact our programs and processes in partnership with business leaders on the People team. If you're interested in a career at National Life, this internship is a great way to begin your journey! KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: The People Center intern will be a vital part of our team and will contribute to our continuing efforts to identify and implement best practices. Key projects include: job posting and resume reviews, recruiting advertising campaign support, content mapping of Servant Leadership, partnership in extended onboarding curriculum and candidate experience. QUALIFICATIONS: Minimum overall GPA of 3.00 Working towards a degree in Human Resources Management, rising Senior preferred Coursework in human resources, organizational development, communications, or related area preferred Proficient in Microsoft tools with interest in learning new tools and systems Excellent written and verbal communication skills. AI Proficiency Expectations: At National Life Group, we view AI as an enabler of human potential. Backed by a $100 million Series B led by Index Ventures, at a $1 billion valuation, we've built a strong foundation for what's next. roles.title: Program Management Intern
roles.description: At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. ROLE OVERVIEW REGENT's Paladin test program is where engineering development, vehicle maintenance, and on-water testing all converge, and this internship sits right at the center of it. You'll build and maintain the schedule that the entire program runs on, working directly with the vehicle and the test team rather than tracking progress from behind a desk. This is a DPM-style role in the truest sense: the milestone tracker isn't a document you update once a week, it's something you actively manage so that engineers, maintenance crews, and test leads are always working from the same plan. You'll join the Engineering & Technology Program Management team, a group that treats planning and tracking as real engineering work, not administrative overhead. Along the way, you'll be taught to see cost and schedule as engineering variables in their own right, a lens that's genuinely valuable whether you're headed toward program leadership or engineering management down the road. If you're someone who gets energized by being in the middle of the action, who sees a plan as something to steer rather than observe, and who wants hands-on exposure to how a real flight test program comes together, we'd love to have you on the team. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own the Master Schedule: You'll build and keep current the milestone tracker that ties together engineering, maintenance, and on-water testing for Paladin. This is a living document you actively manage, not something you dust off weekly. - Get Hands-On with Paladin: You'll spend real time with the vehicle and the test team, not just behind a laptop. Being in the mix is how you'll understand what's actually happening on the ground, not just what's on paper. - Support Vehicle Maintenance: You'll pitch in on maintenance work between test runs, giving you direct insight into what keeps Paladin flight-ready. That proximity to the vehicle is what makes your tracking actually useful. - Know What Complete Really Means: You'll learn to distinguish between a part being ordered, installed, and tested, so your schedule reflects reality rather than optimism. That distinction is what keeps the whole program honest. - Keep the Team Aligned: You'll make sure engineering, maintenance, and test ops are working from the same set of assumptions about what's next. When the plan stays current, the whole program moves faster together. - Launch Your Own Initiatives: You'll take on program initiatives you can plan, manage, and see through to completion. By the end of your term, you'll be able to point to specific projects you drove start to finish. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - Scheduling Tool Fluency: You're comfortable in Smartsheet, MS Project, Jira, or a similar tool. The specific platform matters less than being able to hit the ground organizing the program instead of learning software. - Self-Directed Ownership: You can build and maintain a tracker across multiple workstreams without someone feeding you updates. You treat the plan as something to manage proactively, not react to. - Mechanical Curiosity: Hands-on experience with engines, hulls, or mechanical systems, whether through marine, automotive, or other tinkering, gives you a head start here. A meaningful part of this role involves real vehicle maintenance support. - Technical Grounding: You understand what an engineering or test milestone actually means when it's marked complete. That understanding is what keeps a schedule accurate instead of just looking fine on paper. - Comfort Across Contexts: You're just as comfortable updating a tracker as you are standing next to the vehicle with the test team. You don't need the two worlds kept separate. - Natural Organizational Instinct: You bring structure to dynamic, fast-moving work without slowing it down. You see a plan as something worth actively shaping. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision. - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds. - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat. - Innovative Mindset: You're driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You're passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance. WHAT WE OFFER - Competitive compensation - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team - Daily, free catered lunches - Learning & professional development opportunities - Meaningful projects that make an impact - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact. Equal Opportunity Employer REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

roles.title: Project-/Product-Management Intern (human)
roles.description: YOUR MISSION & CHALLENGES You will work cross-functionally within the Product Development Team and support internal product development as well as all downstream processes throughout the entire product lifecycle: - Supporting Product and Project Management in day-to-day operations across the entire development process and product lifecycle - Preparing and following up on meeting notes, deriving clear action items and work packages - Contributing to the development and industrialization of products – from the concept phase through to series production readiness - Supporting the adherence to quality standards and regulatory requirements throughout the development process - Optimizing processes and tools to continuously increase efficiency and effectiveness - Preparing, structuring, and documenting complex technical and process-related topics - Collaborating closely and coordinating with interdisciplinary teams across mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, software development, procurement, and production - Taking ownership of smaller projects independently and developing own concepts and solutions WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FORWARD TO - Ongoing studies in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Industrial Engineering, Business Informatics, or a comparable degree program with a technical specialization - Strong mechatronic understanding – you think in systems, not in silos - Structured and independent way of working combined with a quick grasp of new topics - Analytical mindset and enthusiasm for questioning and improving processes - Hands-on mentality: You are willing to go the extra mile and take ownership of tasks that may be completely new to you - Very good German and English language skills (minimum C1 level), both written and spoken - Valid Category B driver's license NICE TO HAVE - Initial practical experience in project management, product development, or a technical industrial environment (e.g., through internships or working student positions) - Experience with tools such as Jira, Confluence, PowerPoint, or Word - Passion for robotics, automation, and the development of complex mechatronic products – from initial idea to successful market scaling

roles.title: Recruiting Associate (Internship) - Fort Worth
roles.description: About ITS Logistics Are you ready to build a successful career in a trillion-dollar global industry? ITS Logistics is one of the fastest-growing, exciting logistics companies in the United States providing creative supply chain solutions to Fortune 500 companies.
